title: The LEAF questionnaire: a screening tool for the identification of female athletes at risk for the female athlete triad
authors: Melin A, Tornberg AB, Skouby S, Faber J, Ritz C, Sjodin A, Sundgot-Borgen J
population: Female athletes aged 18-39 training at least 5 times/week; validation in 45 endurance athletes (long-distance running, triathlon)
findings: The 25-item Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire (LEAF-Q) covers injuries and gastrointestinal and reproductive function.

Against measured current EA, menstrual function and bone health in 45 endurance athletes, sensitivity was 78% and specificity 90% for correctly classifying current EA and/or reproductive function and/or bone health.
Reliability and internal consistency were evaluated in a subsample of 37 dancers and endurance athletes.
Authors position it as a complement to validated disordered-eating screening instruments for early detection and intervention.
limitations: Single development study (n = 84; validation n = 45), young adults, validated against a female athlete triad definition, not tested prospectively.
implications: Offer an optional periodic LEAF-Q-style self-screen to female users (plan start and about every 12 weeks is a design default, not from the paper). A positive screen triggers a non-diagnostic clinician prompt and a hold on volume progression.
With sensitivity only 78%, a negative screen must not suppress other REDs flags (missing periods, bone stress injury, recurrent illness).

verification.notes: Crossref matches (BJSM, 2014-02, Melin). Sensitivity/specificity and sample sizes confirmed in Europe PMC abstract (PMID 24563388). Removed unsupported claim about later studies' accuracy.
